Class TaskService

java.lang.Object
com.taskflow.service.TaskService
public class TaskService extends Object
The business logic of the application: create, read, update and delete tasks, change their status, validate input, search / filter / sort, undo deletions and report statistics.

Data structures used

  • LinkedHashMap<Integer, Task> – primary store. Gives O(1) lookup by id while remembering insertion order for stable listing.
  • ArrayDeque used as a stack – the undo history. Push and pop at the head are O(1); it is capped at 20 entries.
  • ArrayList of Runnable – observers notified after every change (the Observer pattern), which keeps the GUI free of business logic.
The service never exposes its internal Task objects; callers always receive copies. Every mutating method saves to the TaskRepository before it notifies observers.

      public Task addTask(String title, String description) throws ValidationException
      Adds a new pending task with medium priority and no due date. This is the minimal "add a task (title and description)" operation required by the lab.
      Parameters:
      title - the title; must not be empty or blank
      description - the description; may be null or empty
      Returns:
      a copy of the newly stored task, including its generated id
      Throws:
      ValidationException - if the title is empty or any field is too long

    • query

      public List<Task> query(String searchText, TaskStatus status, SortOption sort)
      Searches, filters and sorts the tasks in one step. A task matches when its title or description contains the search text (ignoring case) and its status equals the filter. The whole pass is O(n) for matching plus O(m log m) for sorting the m matches.
      Parameters:
      searchText - the text to look for; null or blank matches everything
      status - only tasks with this status; null means all statuses
      sort - the ordering of the result; null means SortOption.NEWEST
      Returns:
      a new list of matching task copies
